text:
dave: RFC idea 1: introduce a small StreamHandle abstraction for the Go SDK to make context ownership and auth/retry behavior explicit. ran into several onboarding issues where users mix background auth refreshers, generator Resume, and backoff retries and end up with confusing hangs or canceled-but-not-closed snapshots.

lina: can you sketch the shape? current Stream(ctx) -> <-chan Token is concise but has these subtle ownership traps.

priya: +1. we keep getting bug reports where support sees long-lived goroutines on customer apps that never called cancel because examples assume ctx propagation is obvious. a thinner API that provides an explicit Close/Stop seems useful.

oscar: proposal sketch:
```go
type AuthRetryPolicy struct {
  MaxAttempts int // 0 = infinite (default)
  InitialBackoff time.Duration
  MaxBackoff time.Duration
  Jitter bool
}

type StreamHandle interface {
  Tokens() <-chan Token // channel you can range over for convenience
  Stop() error         // immediately terminates the stream and any handshakes
  Err() error          // returns terminal error after Stop()/drain
  Meta() map[string]string // metadata like model, request-id for debugging
}

// New API surface
handle := client.Generator("gpt-std").StreamHandle(ctx, Prompt("hi"), OptAuthRetry(AuthRetryPolicy{MaxAttempts:3}))
defer handle.Stop() // recommended for early exit
for tok := range handle.Tokens() { ... }
if err := handle.Err(); err != nil { log.Printf("stream err: %v", err) }
```

emily: I like making Err() explicit so callers can see whether the stream ended cleanly vs was stopped. also the AuthRetryPolicy lets users tune how aggressive client.AuthRefresh() will attempt to re-handshake mid-stream.

dave: ergonomics notes: 1) keep a simple helper that returns a channel directly for one-liners; 2) make Stop() safe to call multiple times; 3) Stop() should cancel any internal per-handshake contexts and close underlying http.Transport connections so blocked dial calls are woken up.

lina: how to handle Resume() patterns? some users call Generator.Resume(state) which spawns worker goroutines and expects the stream to finish later. we need to document how Stop() interacts with Resume and with spawned go routines.

priya: doc plan: update generator README with a "Lifecycle and Ownership" section showing three patterns: (A) simple range-based usage (recommended with defer Stop()), (B) Resume() worker pattern (show WaitGroup + Stop signal), (C) long-running server pattern (expose stream metrics + graceful shutdown hook). add a short snippet for auth-refresh best practices: call client.AuthRefresh() only when no stream handshakes are in-flight or use AuthRetryPolicy{MaxAttempts:0} to avoid mid-handshake restarts.

oscar: tests: we'll add unit tests that simulate an auth endpoint that occasionally returns 401 during handshake and a token rotator. key assertions: goroutine count no-op after repeated Start/Stop, Stop unblocks blocked dialers, Err() surface matches handshake error types, and Channel-shim parity (old Stream(ctx) channel continues to work via a simple shim that wraps StreamHandle.Tokens()).

emily: sampleapps: update go-sampleapps streaming example to use StreamHandle and show graceful shutdown with context + Stop() + wg.Wait(). also add a tiny stress script that runs rotate+start/stop loops to demonstrate reliability.

dave: compatibility: plan to ship StreamHandle in minor release and keep Stream(ctx) channel shim for at least one release cycle. mark channel shim deprecated in docs and show migration snippet.

priya: ops/support: add a metric active_streams_total (labels: client_id, model) and an internal debug endpoint gated behind env var that lists active stream ids and last-handshake-state. will help debug customer "stuck" tickets.

lina: nice. api review: ensure Stop() is deterministic and doesn't race with Next()/Tokens consumption. consider providing a Context() method on StreamHandle that returns an immutable context which is canceled when Stop() runs so helper goroutines can select on it.

dave: good call. we'll add Context() that callers may use for derived operations but note in docs that callers should not cancel it.

emily: i'll add the migration docs and sampleapp edits once the PR is opened. also add a short section in the onboarding guide that emphasizes always pairing streams with Stop()/defer and avoiding auth rotation mid-handshake unless you truly need it.

dave: thanks all 680 i'll open the draft PR with the shim, tests, and docs. assigning to @lina for API review and @priya for runtime tests. will tag sampleapps once CI is green.
